reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
October has a way of stripping things back. The leaves are halfway down, the light gets thin by five, and the big summer plans you had are either done or quietly abandoned. What's left is a Thursday. Groceries. A workout you don't want to do. A conversation you've been putting off. The small, unglamorous architecture of a life.

When I was drinking, Thursdays were something to survive until Friday. Now they're the actual material. I used to think recovery was about the big moments — the anniversaries, the trips I could suddenly take, the mornings I woke up without dread. Those matter. But the real work, the thing that actually built a life I wanted to be in, happened on Thursdays. Showing up for the run. Returning the text. Making dinner instead of ordering it. Going to the meeting when I didn't feel like it.

Durant was paraphrasing Aristotle, and the point holds: you don't become someone in a single decision. You become them through a thousand small ones, most of them boring. Sobriety gave me back the Thursdays. What I do with them is who I'm becoming. Not someday. Today. The ordinary day is not the thing standing between you and your life — it is your life.
reflection.meditation: What small, ordinary thing can I show up for today that past-me would have skipped?

affirmations: I am building my life in the small choices, not waiting for the big ones.
Today I can handle what's in front of me without needing to escape it.
I am becoming someone I actually want to spend a Thursday with.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a quiet October morning and the fact that I remember it. Grateful for the people who stayed while I figured this out, and the ones I've met since who only know the sober version of me. Grateful that today is boring in all the right ways — no crisis, no cover-up, just a day I get to live in.
